A1.justification: Both complete 38-page PDFs describe the same FedGMR work and include Appendices A–H. Text comparison and visual inspection support reliable comparison of the equations, algorithms, tables, figures, and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original federated-learning simulations on FEMNIST, CIFAR-10, ImageNet-100, and StackOverflow, including accuracy, convergence, component ablations, and communication measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and appendix analyses, with an additional numerical summary of the existing FEMNIST comparison in Figure 4.

M1.justification: The restoration trigger, density scheduling, semi-asynchronous coordination, mask-aware aggregation, pruning, and incremental model splitting remain unchanged. Reformatted Algorithms 1–4 preserve the original steps, control flow, and outputs.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four datasets and tasks, IID/non-IID partitions, and bandwidth-heterogeneity scenarios. The new appendix table summarizes an existing FEMNIST experiment.

E2.justification: The main comparator set is unchanged. Figure 4 already evaluates HeteroFL, FjORD, FedRolex, and FIARSE with original, +Aux, and +Aux+GMR configurations in v2; their appearance in v3 Table 9 adds no comparator.

E3.justification: Section 6 and Appendix F retain the same splits, architectures, client settings, training budgets, metrics, and evaluation procedures. The configurations summarized in new Table 9 were already represented in Figure 4.

E4.justification: The component ablations, transfer of GMR to other methods, patience sensitivity, fixed-time restoration, and communication analyses are retained. Table 9 summarizes the existing Figure 4 comparison without introducing a new analytical question or control.

E5.justification: Table 9 newly reports standard deviations for the existing Figure 4 configurations, previously shown as curves with selected means in the prose. Section 6.1 retains its 20-test-evaluation smoothing protocol; no additional independent runs, seeds, or statistical tests are stated.

E6.justification: Table 9 adds exact numerical summaries, including FjORD accuracies of 81.76±0.17, 82.16±0.26, and 82.20±0.29 for Original, +Aux, and +Aux+GMR. The selected HeteroFL, FedRolex, and FIARSE means already quoted in v2 remain unchanged, as do the existing plots and other result tables.

T1.justification: Section 5 and Appendices A and E retain the same mathematical definitions, assumptions, convergence bounds, proofs, and asynchronous perturbation analysis. Reflow around the reformatted algorithms does not change the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about capacity-induced stagnation, gradual restoration, convergence guarantees, and improvements under heterogeneous federated learning.

C2.justification: Appendix H.1 states the separation between auxiliary-workflow gains and restoration gains more clearly, but preserves the interpretation already supported by v2 Figure 4 and its discussion. Applicability qualifications and the discussions of asynchrony, aggregation, and trigger sensitivity remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The implementation descriptions, pruning and transmission routines, hyperparameters, bandwidth allocations, model specifications, data-processing details, and code-access statement are retained. Algorithm cross-reference corrections and pseudocode restyling do not disclose a different implementation.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and reference list are unchanged. Explicitly naming FjORD in the revised Appendix H.1 paragraph does not introduce a new cited work or positioning claim; it already appears in the corresponding v2 figure and main comparisons.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites the awkward Appendix H.1 paragraph, corrects algorithm cross-references in Appendices B–D, revises pseudocode wording, and adds a financial conflict-of-interest disclosure. The overall section structure and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 9 and relocates or renumbers the retained patience, fixed-time restoration, and communication tables as Tables 10–12. Algorithms 1–4 receive new formatting and local page reflow; the plotted content is unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 improves the precision and readability of the existing evidence: Table 9 supplies exact means and standard deviations, Appendix H.1 clearly identifies the comparison configurations, and corrected algorithm references improve navigation. These are useful reporting improvements, while the method, theory, experimental coverage, and main findings remain stable.
